absent-path-and-parent: For the first run, pass an absent state-directory path beneath an existing canonical parent; the wrapper creates that directory privately.
For initial use, choose a new coordinator directory that does not exist under a canonical parent directory that already exists.
no-precreation: Do not pre-create the state directory.
Let the wrapper create the private state directory; do not create it yourself.
ambiguous-state-refusal: An existing directory without `state.json`, even an empty one, is refused because missing metadata may conceal lost active ownership.
If a state directory already exists without `state.json`, leave it intact and expect refusal, including when it is empty.
concurrent-initialization: First-time concurrent initialization can also refuse the losing caller.
If initialization races, the other caller may be refused.
inspect-without-reset: Stop and inspect the original path and any participating processes before an operator chooses a recovery action; the wrapper never resets, deletes or repairs it.
Inspect the original directory and participating processes before any recovery decision; never reset, delete or repair the directory automatically.
